# 1.1.0

## Tagged turns

A turn can now be marked from the assistant action row, the one that already
carries copy, feedback and "branch into a new conversation". The control adds one
entry to that row through `conversation.chat.assistant-actions` rather than
taking the row over, so every built-in action keeps working.

- Click to tag the turn; optionally write a **Markdown** note; click again to
  take the tag off. The note is drawn on the card as bold, italic and inline
  code, built as React elements — nothing a note contains can become markup.
- The tag is stored in the sidecar (`~/.dsh/storages/tree-view/state.json`)
  beside branch names and archive membership. Nothing is appended to the session
  log, which stays append-only.
- It is keyed by the durable message id the action row names, because that is all
  the row has; the host resolves it to a turn while projecting the tree, and
  refuses an id the session never wrote.

## Folding now means "what I came for"

The default fold threshold moves from eight turns to two, the smallest run a fold
can hide, and a tagged turn joins the latest turn on the list of landmarks a fold
may never swallow. A family now draws its origin, its fork points, the turn you
are reading and every turn you tagged, and folds the rest. A stored threshold
that was only ever the old default (8) follows the new one; a number you chose is
kept. `Never` and the toolbar still unfold everything.


## The Tree panel has no toolbar

The five canvas buttons are gone. Two of the things they did were already
settings — the empty-fork filter and the fold threshold — and hiding empty forks
is now stated only there. Collecting every other branch moved onto a branch's own
right-click menu, where the rest of the branch actions live. Centring and
refreshing were conveniences the view already covers: it frames itself when the
layout first lands, and refetches when its cached data goes stale.

## A fold opens an outline, not a drawer

Clicking a fold no longer redraws the canvas. Hovering it lists the turns it
hides — the turn number, what kind of turn it is, and the prompt it carried — and
clicking a row goes to that turn. That is what unfolding was being used for, so
the canvas no longer needs to be able to do it; turning folding off entirely is
still the threshold's "Never".

## The outline names what a turn produced

The fold outline states the open turn and, when it wrote anything, the files it
left behind — as names in inline code, wrapped and capped at four with a count.
The source is the same one DSH's own file row uses: the arguments of successful
`write`, `edit`, and non-`view` `str_replace_editor` calls, in first-seen order
and deduplicated. A call whose result failed contributes nothing.

## Cross-session material is drawn, not just stored

A conversation can be fed by another one. `dsh-subagent` writes both
`agent-message` (one agent addressed this one) and `subagent-settled` (the
runtime reporting what became of a continuable child) as an ordinary user
message whose source names the sender, and the Tree now draws that:

- material from a conversation that is also on the canvas becomes a dashed
  arrow from the sender to the turn that went on with it;
- material from one that is not becomes a `⇠ <handle>` mark on the receiving
  card, with the runtime's account in its tooltip;
- a message that arrived between turns and has not fed one yet — the normal
  case while that turn is still running — hangs off the origin rather than
  being dropped.

The shape was read off a real log rather than guessed: a continuable child was
spawned, and the notice it produced carries `senderSessionId` and no `turn` of
its own, because it lands between turns as input for the next one.

## A tag says where the code stood

Tagging a turn now also records the commit each repository was on at that moment:
the working directory itself and any repository under it, up to three levels down,
skipping the directories that never hold one. The turn's card shows a short commit
and the path for each, with the full commit and branch in the tooltip.

The reading is taken when the tag is written, not when the tree is drawn — a tag is
a claim about that turn, and the working directory keeps moving after it. `.git` is
read directly: a loose ref, a packed ref, a detached HEAD, and the `gitdir:` pointer
a worktree or submodule uses are all handled without shelling out to git.

The fold outline no longer repeats the turn number: the rule the pointer is on
already says which turn it is.

## The cross-session layer has a switch

One control stands on the panel's left edge and turns the cross-session layer
off: the dashed arrows and the marks a sender that is not on the canvas leaves
behind. It is on by default, and the choice is remembered.

The control is a glyph, not a label — a mesh of three nodes — with `aria-label`
and a tooltip carrying the words, so the rail stays narrow.

The switch reaches past the drawing. A turn that took material in is a landmark
while that layer is shown, which is what keeps it on the canvas instead of inside
a fold; hide the layer and it folds back with the stretch it sits in. A layer
nobody is drawing is no reason to hold the canvas open.

## Fixed

An audit of both halves turned up these. Each one is covered by a test that was
checked against the old code, except where noted.

- **One unreadable session log no longer takes the family with it.** Reading a
  log that is truncated or shaped in a way this build rejects used to reject the
  whole `GET /tree-view`, so a single bad file made every other version of the
  conversation disappear from the panel with a 409. The family walk now draws
  that version without its turns, which is what the orphan scan already did, and
  says so once in the log.
- **A native DSH fork keeps its whole ancestry.** A fork is seeded with its
  parent's entire log and writes no version marker of its own, so the last marker
  in its log belongs to the parent. The ancestor walk assumed the last marker was
  the session's own and counted back one from there, which dropped a generation
  and hung every effect on the wrong session — visible when an ancestor had been
  deleted, where a whole version went missing from the tombstone chain. Markers
  name the session that wrote them, so the walk looks them up by name now and
  only falls back to counting for markers written before they carried a name.
- **A deleted ancestor no longer blocks an edit.** The same walk stopped on a
  hole in the tree when resolving where to attach a branch, and a hole has no
  record to load. It now treats that as the end of the walk, so editing a version
  below a deleted parent works, as the canvas already suggested it would.
- **Cross-session references appear when they arrive.** The layer that draws the
  dashed arrows was memoised on the layout, and a link lands on a node whose id,
  parent and path are all unchanged — a sender already on the canvas hands
  material in. The arrow was never drawn and, because the mark filter reads the
  same memo, the mark on the receiving card was suppressed with it. It is keyed on
  the links now.
- **Two hand-ins from one sender no longer collide.** The host emits one link per
  message, so a sender can contribute twice before the next turn begins; both the
  arrow and the card mark were keyed by the sender alone, which handed React the
  same key twice.
- **An image block with no attachment survives one that has an attachment.** When
  the host's gallery handled part of a message, the blocks it could not show were
  dropped silently instead of keeping the placeholder.
- **A malformed version marker refuses with a reason.** A `message-tree/version`
  event missing its data or its inverse produced a raw `TypeError` on the path
  that resolves an edit's attach point; it now reports the same refusal the tree
  projection reports. *(Not covered by a test: reachable only with a foreign
  marker.)*
- **A failed tool result is recognised wherever its error block sits.** Produced
  files were read off `content[0]` alone, so a failure carried in a later block
  still reported the file as produced.
- **Unarchiving reports whether it changed anything.** `show()` answered
  `changed: true` unconditionally, even when the queued write found the session
  already unarchived and did nothing.

## A fold is a circle

A folded stretch used to be drawn as a card the width of a turn, with a title, a
chevron and a stack of offset sheets behind it. It is a circle now, with the
number of turns it hides inside: a stretch of twenty turns becomes a point on the
line instead of a card the size of the ones it stands for, which is the whole
reason the fold exists.

Everything that made it usable is still there. Hovering opens the outline of the
turns inside, and the tooltip still says whether the run is the opening every
version shares or a stretch one branch carries on with. Those two are told apart
on the canvas by the ring — dashed for the shared opening, solid for the run —
since there is no room left for the words.

The slot grid and the layout are untouched, so nothing else on the canvas moved.
Only the node's own box shrank to the circle, and the edges that meet it now
attach to the ring rather than to the corners of a card that is no longer there.

## Also

- A user message whose content shape this build cannot draw now says so instead
  of rendering an empty bubble, and reports the block types it received once.
- `contentBlocks` recovers a plain string and blocks nested one level down, so
  additive host changes keep rendering without a notice.
- Removed `_wrap-client.mjs`, a superseded duplicate of
  `scripts/build-client.mjs` that nothing referenced.
- The client source moved off the repository root: `plugin.client.js` is now
  `src/client.js`. `lib/` holds what DSH loads — the host modules and the built
  bundle — so the rule is one line: edit `lib/*.js` and `src/client.js`, never
  `lib/client.js`.
- The tests are grouped by the half they cover, `test/host/` and `test/client/`,
  instead of nineteen files in one directory.
